- The flagship rank-1 modal fit (examples [09](09-rank1-modal-mimo.qmd)/[10](10-srm-hsts.qmd)) run on a **real reduced aLIGO quad** — realistic multi-stage dynamics between the lumped teaching plants and the heavy compiled twin.

[![Launch in Binder](https://mybinder.org/badge_logo.svg)](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/CaltechExperimentalGravity/system_ident/HEAD?urlpath=lab/tree/docs/examples/11-reduced-quad.ipynb)  ·  runs live, no install (the [in-browser demo](interactive.qmd) is instant)

The earlier MIMO examples fit a lumped teaching plant ([09](09-rank1-modal-mimo.qmd)) or the
compiled-CDS twin through its real loops ([10](10-srm-hsts.qmd), `freeze: true`, local-only).
This page runs the same method on the **realistic middle**: the digital twin's **modal-truncation
reduced** aLIGO quadruple suspension — the full 1483-state state-space cut to a faithful
**59-state** model over the control band — committed in the package as
`system_ident/models/quad_reduced_50hz.npz`. Because the reduced model is just `(A,B,C,D)`, the
plant FRF `G(f)=C(2πif·I−A)⁻¹B+D` and the whole campaign are **pure numpy** — so, unlike the
compiled-twin pages, this one is not frozen: it re-runs in CI and in Binder.


## The plant and the campaign

The reduced quad has four stages (M0 → L1 → L2 → L3). We identify its **yaw chain** — drive the
yaw actuator of each stage, read the yaw displacement of each — a 4×4 open-loop MIMO with four
well-separated rigid-body modes (0.6–3.0 Hz). One Pintelon–Schoukens multisine per actuator is
driven through the numpy-only `ReducedPlantBackend`; the per-bin matrix recovery `G = Y·X⁻¹`
returns the open-loop 4×4 FRF (the backend synthesizes the steady-state response exactly, so a
long record costs nothing).

```{python}
#| code-summary: "What resolution / record does the campaign use?"
display(Markdown(
    f"The campaign drives **{h.n_lines}** excited lines and observes a **{h.record_s:.0f} s** "
    f"record ({int(rq.NPER)} periods) — a long record needed to resolve these high-Q modes, but "
    f"the reduced plant is evaluated in the frequency domain so it computes in seconds. The four "
    f"yaw modes are then found from the recovered FRF (no oracle) and fit jointly."))
```

## Through-resonance recovery

The rank-1 modal fit shares one set of poles across the 4×4 and threads cleanly **through** the
resonances where the per-bin inverse (grey) scatters. One diagonal (`G[0,0]`, M0→M0) and one
off-diagonal (`G[0,3]`, L3→M0) element, with the fit's ±1σ band and the reduced plant's analytic
truth:

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Through-resonance recovery — G[0,0] and G[0,3]"
rq.through_resonance_fig()
```

## Modal recovery vs the plant's exact modes

The reduced model's own eigen-modes are the ground truth. The recovered `(f₀, Q)` sit on them with
a Cramér–Rao envelope:

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Modal frequency recovery — fit − truth with the CRB"
rq.modal_recovery_fig()
```

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Recovered yaw modes — truth vs fit ± σ"
display(rq.modal_table())
```

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Headline numbers"
display(Markdown(
    f"The joint fit recovers all **{h.n_modes}** yaw modes of the reduced quad: median |Δf₀| vs "
    f"the exact modes = **{h.df_med:.4f}%** (a part in 10⁵), median |ΔQ| = **{h.q_med:.1f}%**, "
    f"with a trustworthy CRB. Everything on this page — the plant, the campaign, the fit — is "
    f"numpy/scipy, so it ran just now in CI (or in your browser) with no compiled twin."))
```

## What this shows

The flagship joint-MIMO modal method, unchanged, on a **real reduced aLIGO quad** rather than a
lumped teaching plant or the local-only compiled twin. The frequencies of the four yaw
rigid-body modes come back to a part in 10⁵ and their (model-set) Q to a percent, all in portable
numpy — the realistic, reproducible middle the reduced models were brought in to provide. The
same machinery drives the [SRM demo](10-srm-hsts.qmd) through real production loops on the twin;
here it runs anywhere.
